answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to pass periodic proof-of-personhood checks tied to a single scarce credential, like a marble token earned only after verified work. New identities start with narrow permissions, like a trellis that supports growth only along one verified stem, and earn wider access gradually as attestors confirm real contributions. An attacker crossing the canyon between one fake identity and thousands would need to pass each check separately, making mass forgery far costlier than running one honest agent.
